statement: Unmodified cut_bounds commit 6b720fe57bfe2a3c8fffc51521d00b31011aa1a3 reproduces the published positive-rho certificate: h_+^2 <= 3.99929096609, worst slab [0.38625,0.3875], 90 accepted slabs / 150 attempts.
assumptions: Unmodified published script; dependency and command versions in reproduction_metadata.json.
gap: Reproduction of a published certificate, not a new theorem or independent audit.

statement: Uncertified numerical instrument: the literal published-center h_+ crosses 2 at rho approximately 0.43251274; the mean-zero J_+-weighted operator norm crosses 2 at approximately 0.44101422. At rho=.4, HS/operator=1.0094343378. Three root refinements and independent J/K/centering controls agree as logged.
assumptions: Heilman Appendix A kernels (145),(148),(149), fixed binary64 center (150).
Gauss-Legendre Nystrom quadrature on finite x domains; rho sampled on [.4,.95].
Weighted mean-zero projection is enforced; arithmetic is binary64.
gap: No rigorous discretization, tail or root enclosure; no new noise-stability theorem.

statement: At each requested rho in {.45,.5,.6,.7,.8,.9}, 81 radial coupling values and the saved scalar/simplex grids show no violation above 1e-10 of the stronger scalar bound, (139), or (142). Maximum signed (139) residual is 6.66e-16. Lemma A.2 and Corollary A.3 are already stated for every a>=0, independent of a rho restriction.
assumptions: Scalar p,q in [0,1]; vector p,q in Delta_3.
Each a grid spans 0 to 98*rho/(1-rho^2), with logarithmic small-a points.
Bessel-series truncation and all arithmetic are uncertified binary64; selected truncations doubled.
sources: 2608.00333v1 Lemma A.2 pp.38-40 and Corollary A.3 p.40
gap: Finite grids do not prove a universal inequality or exclude failures between tested points; source theorem is attributed, not a new proof.

statement: A symmetric weighted kernel dominated on radial cells by a symmetric nonnegative finite matrix B has full operator norm at most max_i (Bv)_i/v_i + sqrt(tau), where v>0 is any exact witness and tau bounds the squared-kernel integral outside the finite square. Applied to Heilman Appendix A this bounds the same constrained simplex operator.
assumptions: All entries and sums are outward-rounded upper bounds uniformly on a rho slab.
tau encloses the entire complement of [0,L]^2.
The original kernel is symmetric; B is entrywise nonnegative and symmetric; v is strictly positive.
gap: No numerical extension asserted by this lemma; the computation and source reduction must separately pass. Basis differs from the assigned Laguerre suggestion.

statement: For n>=2, every measurable balanced partition of R^n into three Gaussian cells has rho-noise stability at most that of the standard simplex partition for every rho in [1/10,803/2000]. The new weighted-operator certificate covers [2/5,803/2000] with upper bound 1.998371111346653 < 2.
assumptions: The source dimension-reduction and aligned-arc reduction in Heilman arXiv:2608.00333v1 Appendix A.
Recorded exact dyadic centers and witnesses; outward-rounded Arb/binary64 enclosures and complete analytic tails.
gap: Independent source-level audit pending. This prefix is smaller than the requested 0.42/0.43 target.

statement: If ||PTP||<=lambda and ||T-PTP||_HS^2<=tau for an orthogonal projection P, then ||T||<=sqrt(lambda^2+tau). Combining a directed positive radial-cell matrix with the complete source outside tail therefore certifies the same weighted simplex operator.
assumptions: T is bounded; the omitted block is Hilbert-Schmidt.
Finite matrix entries and final arithmetic are outward upper bounds.

statement: For every n>=2, every balanced measurable three-cell Gaussian partition has rho-noise stability at most the standard simplex partition for every rho in [1/10,43/100]. The new interval [2/5,43/100] is certified by a full-operator bound below 2.
assumptions: Three measurable partition cells, each of measure 1/3
gap: Awaiting independent audit of the analytic reduction, interval implementation, and exact claim version. Uses radial cells rather than a direct application of the sphere-valued Laguerre theorem.
